ai.description: This gecko reaches 45 mm in snout-vent length. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include keeled ventral scales and a lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis assamensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, smooth ventral scales and the absence of precloacal pores in males.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis assamensis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found on tree trunks or rocky surfaces at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Assamese Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis assamensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis assamensis* is endemic to the Northeast Indian states of Assam and Meghalaya, inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 100 and 800 meters.
